One should look at what is actually causing the pain, which is a mechanical misalignment, due to improper use. The improper use being likely long-term "activity" in positions or postures the body is not designed for. An example being truck drivers who often get back problems. We're not designed to sit in a disproportionate length of time. Many probably common sitting postures may be particularly bad when part of an extended habit.

I threw my back out from sitting in a slouched position, a habit of sliding down in an office chair, suspending the lower back between the butt and the mid-back, instead of a more vertical healthy posture. So I actually threw the back out while lifting some rather light weights, but I understood the real reason was the sitting posture, because it had been giving me some milder repeating pains for a while, which made me correct my posture intermittently. I believe this is very typical. It's your habitual poor postures that permanently stretches ligaments in the back that should naturally be more tight, and this allows for any random event to kick the disc in that area out of position, hence some level of hernia.

I studied a bit, and thought of this in a mechanical sense, realizing that the only thing to improve the actual cause would be mechanical manipulation. The purpose being to realign the vertebra's into their ideal positions. So I understood I needed an inversion table for this purpose. Stretching the back like a string will elongate and produce maximum space for the discs. More space will necessarily cause a suction effect on them, since they are closed fluid bodies, which means any herniation will be sucked in / forced to retract. While the discs are fluid in a sense, they are more accurately not fluid, but viscous. This means two things. It takes some time for them to respond to stretch, and after being stretched, they maintain their new "posture" for an extended period of time.

So while speculating on this, and looking for an inversion table, which wasn't readily available in my area, I improvised one, making a decline plank off the back of a couch. I can only say the relief from that when you have serious back pain was unquestionable. This was sufficient for me, but I must warn it's not easy to get into position, not easy to get up, and difficult to construct some level of tension at the feet end, as you need to fix the feet or knees in order for the upper body to have something to pull against. The spine must be subject to a real force where the torso hangs against fixed feet or hips. And I was not old, so if your old, this may be even harder to manage. Hence I advise a proper inversion table.

As for the table, I advise not to buy the cheapest one. It should be comfortable, steady, and well constructed. You may hang inverted for like 30 minutes, and if you got serious problems maybe you need to use it daily or even multiple times a day. So you don't need the top models, but I wouldn't buy the cheapest. I looked at Ironman IFT 3000 (not 4000 with bumps), or Ironman Gravity 3000 or 4000, which I think looked rather good. Also M-Extender looked very good.

This mechanical manipulation should take the slack out and relieve the pain. But if you want to improve into a state where you reduce your dependency on the inversion table, you also need to find out what habits of yours are the likely cause, putting your back in a position outside its ideal range. As I said, this is likely not heavy lifts, but minor-to-medium misalignments over extended periods of time, that permanently makes the various ligaments, of which there are many, weak and lengthened, allowing the discs the opening that facilitates discs to herniate. It's basically posture, which takes some dedication to adjust. But when you truly understand this is your problem, dedication shouldn't be a problem.

Still, while understanding and correcting posture is important, it's my belief that this may likely not be enough when having reached the state of permanent/regular pain. Spinal extension is required, and will at least be much faster. It's instant pain-relief, but by true manipulation of the actual mechanical cause.
